importCycleAnalysis.theEdgeThatCreatesIt: matchJournalAuthority.ts must import a VALUE (resolveCombatJournalAuthorityMode) from combatJournalAuthorityEnabled.ts for getCombatJournalAuthorityMode() to consult the arm. If the new module also imports the VALUE COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE back from matchJournalAuthority.ts, the two modules form a runtime cycle. The plan is to build the charter's preferred zero-argument shape (Option A) first and MEASURE it by running the pin plus the full `src/lib/multiplayer/server` suite; if any load-order failure or an oxlint/tsc cycle complaint appears, fall back to Option B (the production constant passed in as a parameter, leaving only a type-only edge). The red receipt records which was measured and which shipped.

Exports COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_E2E_ENV = 'MEKSTATION_E2E_COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE'; e2eCombatJournalAuthorityMode(): CombatJournalAuthorityMode | null returning 'shadow' or 'enabled' only when process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE === 'true' AND the key holds exactly one of those two literals (either key alone, an absent key, or any other value yields null); resolveCombatJournalAuthorityMode(): CombatJournalAuthorityMode returning the production constant when it is not 'off', else the e2e arm, else 'off'.

design.getterChange: getCombatJournalAuthorityMode() becomes `return combatJournalAuthorityModeOverride ?? resolveCombatJournalAuthorityMode();`. The test override keeps winning, so every existing suite that drives shadow/enabled through _setCombatJournalAuthorityModeForTests is unaffected.
design.constantsKept: COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE and COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED stay exported and stay 'off' / false. Every existing pin of them stays green by construction, because this unit does not touch their values.
design.serverMatchHostSeam: ServerMatchHost.ts:451-452 currently derives the bootstrap default inline. That expression moves, unchanged in meaning, into a small exported helper in the SAME file, and `create` calls it. The helper is what the pin asserts. See seamMeasurement for why the host itself is not the seam.
design.seamMeasurement: Measured, not assumed: (1) ServerMatchHost.create's only reachable entry needs a full IMatchHostBootstrap -- mapRadius, turnLimit, SeededRandom, an IHexGrid, player/opponent units and a gameUnits roster -- plus a created match row and a poll until two events persist; the existing makeHost helper in __tests__/journalAuthorityAdmission.test.ts spans lines 140-172 and leans on three more fixture builders (createMinimalGrid, twoSidedRoster, makeMeta). (2) Worse, the default is NOT observable through that fixture: with the mode override at 'enabled' and bootstrap.journalAuthority omitted, the getter form yields requested=true, but resolveJournalAuthorityForNewMatch then calls isJournalAuthorityBaselineStore(store), and InMemoryMatchStore is not one, so it returns {enabled:false, refusal:null} -- byte-identical to the constant form's requested=false path (admitJournalAuthority returns {kind:'inert'} at journalAuthorityAdmission.ts:177). Distinguishing the two at host level therefore needs a SQLite-backed baseline store, which is a large fixture by any reading. The charter's stated fallback -- 'pin the derived expression through a small exported helper and say so' -- is taken, and this is the saying-so.
design.mutantM3underThisDesign: M3 ('ServerMatchHost.ts:452 reads the constant again') is applied to the helper body in ServerMatchHost.ts, which IS the expression that lived at line 452. The residual the helper cannot cover is stated as a non-claim in the local receipt: a future edit that bypasses the helper at the call site is not caught by this pin.

risksForTheParent: This unit ARMS the combat-journal mode; it does not flip it. The two genesis clauses stay unprovable until U15b forwards MEKSTATION_E2E_COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE and NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE through the qc-core env and playwright.config.ts, and the parent runs the ladder there. Nothing in this lane demonstrates a genesis row being written.

The arm widens what an e2e process can turn on. The two-key law is the whole mitigation: a production process without NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE='true' cannot reach 'shadow' or 'enabled' through this path no matter what the mode key holds, and an e2e process that does not set the mode key gets 'off'. The pin is what holds that law; there is no runtime guard beyond it.

A stale environment is now load-bearing in a way it was not before. If a CI or developer shell leaks both keys, combat journal authority silently arms for that process. The pin's afterEach restores both keys so no jest suite can inherit the arm, but that discipline does not extend outside jest.

The unknown-value case fails CLOSED to 'off' by design. An operator who types MEKSTATION_E2E_COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE=on or =1 gets silence, not an error. That is the safe direction but it is also a debugging trap for U15b; the pin documents it and nothing logs it.

The ServerMatchHost helper pin cannot observe the create call site itself (see design.seamMeasurement). A future edit that reads the constant at the call site instead of calling the helper is not caught by this unit's pin.
The unit's review class is `authority`, so the PR is Lane-B gated and cannot merge on Lane A alone; PK-u15a-ruling does not exist in units.json yet.
